data.exact_reserve_text: There was a positive run-off deviation in the year of GBP 12.2m made up GBP 15.1m Accident and Health, GBP 1.3m Marine and GBP 0.9m Energy and GBP 9.3m discontinued which was offset by an adverse deviation of GBP 14.4m in Casualty.

prior_year_events.impact_description: a reserve reinsurance, became effective at 30th June 2023. This resulted in all 2021 & prior underwriting year business (excluding Space policies and a single Casualty policy called Themis) being reinsured to a limit of 130% of the ceded reserves.

remaining exposure to COVID has reduced significantly due to the LPT. The remaining net reserves amount to GBP 0.9m, almost all of which relate to the outbreak of Covid in Japan during 2022. We no longer consider COVID a significant uncertainty.

named_events.loss_description: The transaction covered loss reserves ceded initially estimated at $190 million as of the valuation date of September 30, 2022, which were reduced to $144 million as of June 30, 2023, as a result of paid losses and favourable prior accident year reserve development recognised during the interim period. All regulatory approvals and closing conditions were met and the transaction closed and incepted on June 30, 2023. The 2023 LPT covered approximately $147 million of loss reserves. The premium payable to Pallas Reinsurance of $127 million is on a funds withheld basis and has been recognised as a liability on the balance sheet. The resulting gain has been recognised in the income statement for the period to December 31, 2023.

In the current year, our remaining exposure to COVID has reduced significantly due to the LPT. The remaining net reserves amount to GBP 0.9m, almost all of which relate to the outbreak of Covid in Japan during 2022. We no longer consider COVID a significant uncertainty.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 12.238 million in 2023, representing a 6.18% reduction of opening gross reserves. This was driven by a positive run-off deviation of GBP 12.2m, which comprised favorable development in Accident and Health (GBP 15.1m), Marine (GBP 1.3m), Energy (GBP 0.9m), and Discontinued (GBP 9.3m), partially offset by an adverse deviation (strengthening) of GBP 14.4m in Casualty. The Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) transaction, effective June 30, 2023, reinsured 2021 and prior underwriting year business, significantly impacting prior year reserves and reducing COVID-19 exposure. Claims inflation continued to be a factor, leading to additional IBNR being held for excess claims inflation.
